text: When did a friendship in your life truly start, in your memory?
evaluation: Friends often disagree on the moment. The gap is usually charming.

text: What did you think of a close friend before you became friends?
evaluation: First impressions are surprisingly portable. Sit with what you initially saw.

text: What is one thing you have never said out loud about why a particular friendship matters to you?
evaluation: What stays unsaid is often what is felt most. The reflexive 'oh stop' robs the offering.

text: What is one thing you have thought about telling a friend and decided not to?
evaluation: The choice not to say it is also data — and may be the right choice.

text: What is the most generous thing a friend has done for you that you suspect they don't think you noticed?
evaluation: The asymmetry of noticing is the relationship. Worth surfacing.

text: What is the most generous thing you have done for a friend that you don't think they noticed?
evaluation: Sit with it without resentment. Just register the asymmetry.

text: When have you let a friend down, and did you ever name it to them?
evaluation: If the answer is no, the second part is the real question.

text: When did a friend let you down in a way you never named to them?
evaluation: Asking it of yourself often relieves more than you expect.

text: What do you trust a particular friend with that you do not trust your other friends with?
evaluation: Specific. Not 'everything'.

text: What do you trust some friends with that you do not trust a closer one with — and is that yours to fix?
evaluation: An honest map of friendship's edges. Sometimes the answer is 'no, it's just shape'.

text: What is one thing about your life you suspect a friend doesn't take seriously?
evaluation: Sit with it; consider whether you have ever asked them to.

text: What is one thing about your life that a friend takes more seriously than you do yourself?
evaluation: Often funny, occasionally sobering. Useful to know either way.

text: What is the kindest interpretation of a habit of a friend's that bothers you?
evaluation: Trains charity. The ability to find one is itself the answer.

text: What habit of a friend's is genuinely a problem, no matter how charitably you read it?
evaluation: Pair with ft013. Take the answer at face value.

text: What is one thing you have stopped sharing with a friend, even though they would want to know?
evaluation: Often a small drift, easily reversed once named.

text: What is one thing you have started sharing with a friend that you would not have years ago?
evaluation: An audit of a friendship's deepening. Often the most encouraging answer of the session.

text: When did you last feel like the lesser friend in a particular friendship?
evaluation: Friendships rotate roles. Inability to recall any feels false.

text: When did you last feel like the carrying friend?
evaluation: Pair with ft017. Imbalance over time is information.

text: What do you want from a friendship that you have not asked for?
evaluation: Specific asks beat general grievances every time.

text: What does a friend offer you that you have not asked for, but want?
evaluation: Quiet generosity rarely gets named. Name it.

text: What does a friend do, when you are in a hard time, that helps?
evaluation: Specifics: presence, distraction, problem-solving, food, silence. Don't generalise.

text: What does a friend do, when you are in a hard time, that doesn't help — even though they think it does?
evaluation: Sit with whether you have ever told them.

text: What do you wish a friend would ask, when you are in a hard time?
evaluation: Save the answer. Use it the next time someone you love is in one.

text: What do you wish a friend would never ask, when you are in a hard time?
evaluation: Common offenders: 'are you eating?', 'have you tried...'.

text: Who in your life knows a version of you that your closest friend doesn't?
evaluation: Healthy adults have multiple knowers. The question is whether you can sit with that without guilt.

text: Who in your life knows none of the version of you that a particular friend does?
evaluation: The reverse. Maps the social geometry.

text: What do you envy in a friend, that you have never said?
evaluation: Naming envy in a safe friendship defuses it. Don't reassure yourself too quickly out of it.

text: What does a friend have that you would never want?
evaluation: The reverse of envy. Often funnier and equally honest.

text: What do you envy in your shared friends?
evaluation: Triangulates more honestly than asking direct envy.

text: What part of you has a close friend never met?
evaluation: Some friends meet only certain rooms of a person. Names the closed doors.

text: What part of a friend have you never met that you have guessed at?
evaluation: Your guess is often striking. Worth quietly checking next time you see them.

text: When did you last lie to a friend, even small?
evaluation: The 'even small' frame opens the answer. White lies are still data.

text: When did a friend last lie to you in a way you noticed but did not name?
evaluation: Sit with why the moment slid past you. The asymmetry of knowing is the lesson.

text: What do you wish friends did for each other that yours haven't yet?
evaluation: Often surfaces a small ritual you have wanted to suggest.

text: What do you wish friends didn't do that you have been doing for one out of habit?
evaluation: Permission to drop the obligation.

text: What is the friendship in your life you most quietly admire?
evaluation: Doesn't have to be one of yours. Often reveals the model you carry.

text: What is the friendship in your life that has hurt the most?
evaluation: Big question. Probably needs space afterwards.

text: What is the friendship that ended that you still carry?
evaluation: Many adults have one. Most rarely talk about it.

text: What did you learn from a friendship that ended badly?
evaluation: If the lesson is purely about the other person, the lesson isn't done.

text: What did you do, in a friendship that ended, that you would do differently?
evaluation: Accountability question. Watch for whether the ownership is genuine or performed.

group: the kind of friend you are
text: What kind of friend are you when life is going well for you?
evaluation: Many are good in others' crises and absent in their own bloom. Honest answers are rare.

group: the kind of friend you are
text: What kind of friend are you when life is going badly for you?
evaluation: Pair with ft041. Together they sketch the whole shape.

group: the kind of friend you are
text: What kind of friend are you when life is going well for them and badly for you?
evaluation: The most revealing of the three.

text: Who do you call first with bad news, and who calls you?
evaluation: Specific names. Asymmetry is information.

text: Who do you call first with good news, and who calls you?
evaluation: Different people often hold the two.

text: What do you do for friends that you would want them to know is effort?
evaluation: Quiet labour deserves naming. Don't perform the gratitude — just register it.

text: What do friends do for you that you suspect costs more than they show?
evaluation: Reciprocity check. Useful for adjusting the next month, not for guilt.

text: What is one promise you made to a friend that you have kept?
evaluation: Builds the floor. Specifics please.

text: What is one promise you made to a friend that you have broken?
evaluation: If the answer is 'I never break promises', that itself is the answer.

text: What does a long friendship require that a new one doesn't?
evaluation: Your thesis on longevity. Listen for whether maintenance or grace dominates.

text: What does a new friendship require that a long one doesn't?
evaluation: Often: more energy, less assumption.

text: What is one thing you have been protecting a friend from?
evaluation: Sometimes protection is wisdom; sometimes it is contempt. Listen for tone in your own answer.

text: What is one thing you have stopped protecting a friend from, and was that the right call?
evaluation: Names the maturation of the friendship.

text: When did a friendship in your life feel most equal?
evaluation: Equality doesn't mean sameness. Listen for what the moment had.

text: When did a friendship in your life feel most unequal?
evaluation: All friendships go uneven. The question is what was learned.

text: What do you want a friend to do less of?
evaluation: Direct. Sit with whether you have asked them.

text: What do you want a friend to do more of?
evaluation: Counterpart. Always pair.

text: What is the unfinished conversation between you and a friend?
evaluation: There's almost always one. The naming is most of the work.

text: What conversation between you and a friend did you finish well, that you should remember you can?
evaluation: Recall is repair. Reminds you of your capacity.

text: What is one thing about a close friend you have assumed for years that may no longer be true?
evaluation: Friendships ossify around old maps. Refresh on purpose.

text: What is one thing you have believed about a close friend for years that may no longer be true?
evaluation: Mirror. Ask the same of yourself — the assumptions friends carry about each other are usually mutual.

text: What part of your life are you keeping smaller than it is, around a particular friend?
evaluation: Some friends shrink themselves to keep an old equilibrium. Worth naming.

text: What part of your life have you kept smaller than it actually is around your friends in general?
evaluation: Most of us minimise something around the people closest to us. Naming what is the work.

text: What is one thing a friend has grown into that you have not yet caught up to?
evaluation: Sit with it. Update your model. Tell them what you noticed.

text: What is one thing you have grown into that a friend has not caught up to?
evaluation: Counterpart. Both can be true at once.

text: What kind of friend do you want to be that you haven't been able to?
evaluation: Aspiration. Often constrained by life conditions, not character.

text: What kind of friend have you been that you no longer want to be?
evaluation: Permission to retire an old role.

text: What is one practice you would adopt to keep a friendship alive?
evaluation: Small, specific, repeatable. A monthly walk beats a yearly grand gesture.

text: What is one practice you would retire from a friendship?
evaluation: Inertia maintains rituals long after they earn their keep.

text: What is one moment in a friendship you would remind yourself of when you doubt your own worth?
evaluation: Save the answer. Use it.

text: What is one moment in a friendship you would remind a friend of when they doubt you?
evaluation: Reciprocal. Build a small mutual archive.

text: What in a particular friendship would you be wrong to take for granted?
evaluation: Names what to actively maintain.

text: What in a particular friendship is, frankly, easy to take for granted because it just works?
evaluation: Light. Often funny. Don't over-analyse.

text: What is one quiet kindness you could do for a friend this month?
evaluation: Tee up a concrete answer. Then do it.

text: What is one quiet kindness you would like a friend to do for you this month, that you wouldn't see coming?
evaluation: Fantasy is allowed here. The naming itself is sweet.

text: What is one change in a friend's life you would be the wrong person to lean into?
evaluation: Realistic limits. No friendship covers everything.

text: What change in a friend's life would you be the right person to lean on for?
evaluation: Names the specific gift you carry. Don't deflect it.

text: What is one secret a friend keeps that you wish they didn't?
evaluation: Sometimes the wish to know is curiosity, not love. Be honest about which.

text: What is one secret you keep that you wish a friend didn't have to keep with you?
evaluation: Permission to release something into a friend's keeping.

text: What part of your week are you proudest of?
evaluation: A mid-session lift. Honest pride is rarer than performed pride.

text: What part of your week are you embarrassed about?
evaluation: Often funny. Always disarming.

text: What is the most useful thing a friend has ever said to you?
evaluation: If you remember it word for word, that is the gift. Note the source as much as the line.

text: What is the most useless piece of advice a friend has ever given you?
evaluation: If you can laugh telling it, the friendship is healthy.

text: Who in your shared circle do you trust least, and have you ever named why — even to yourself?
evaluation: Heavy. Only sit with this if you can hold the answer.

text: Who in your shared circle do you trust most, and do your friends underrate them?
evaluation: An update worth taking seriously.

text: What is one thing you have been waiting for the right moment to ask a friend?
evaluation: This is the moment.

text: What is one thing you have been waiting for the right moment to tell a friend?
evaluation: Same — give the moment.

text: What is one apology you owe a friend that you have not given?
evaluation: Don't write the answer unless you intend to give it.

text: What is one apology a friend owes you that they have not given?
evaluation: Sit with whether it actually still matters to you.

text: What is one thing you do that earns a friend's respect?
evaluation: Name it without deflecting. Then ask the next.

text: What is one thing you do that may erode a friend's respect, even slightly?
evaluation: Brave question. Take your own answer at face value.

text: What in a shared past with a friend do you remember differently than they do?
evaluation: Often delightful. Memory is collaborative; the gaps are part of the friendship.

text: What story do you tell about a friend that they have never heard you tell?
evaluation: Tells you how someone close appears in their own absence — and what you choose to keep of them.

text: What story does a friend tell about you that you wish they would retire?
evaluation: We curate each other publicly. Refresh the curation.

text: What is one piece of advice from a friend you took that turned out well?
evaluation: Quiet credit. Sit with it without bragging.

text: What is one piece of advice from a friend you took that turned out badly?
evaluation: Sit with it without re-justifying. Just acknowledge.

text: What is one piece of advice from a friend you didn't take that you should have?
evaluation: Often funny. Don't gloat at yourself.

text: What is one piece of advice from a friend you didn't take that you were right not to?
evaluation: The friend you can ignore is the friend you can keep.

text: What is one thing you want a particular friend to know, that you have never said?
evaluation: Closing-friendly. Often the line of the night arrives here.

text: What is one thing you would like to be asked again in six months?
evaluation: Plants the next session. Save the answer; calendar the question.
